messages:
Samir: Heads up — us-west GPU pool spiked to ~95% for ~20m. A bunch of high-qps keys hit the admission layer and started getting immediate 429s. Looks like small, chatty requests + a few big batching jobs. infra-bot also fired a saturation alert :warning:

Maya: Any logs/ids? which keys/orgs are hottest?

Samir: quick snippet from the admission log:```[2026-03-18T12:23:45Z] admit key=org-42 tok_avail=0 refill_rate=0.0/s alloc_gpus=2 backlog_ms=1300 action=drop```

Samir: Top offenders: org-42, org-acme, key=svc-frontend (very chatty), plus one internal loadtest that sneaked through.

Li: This is the usual trouble — fixed bucket caps that ignore current fleet capacity. Proposal: move to a capacity-proportional refill model + local short queue (soft spillover) for small bursts. Refill formula idea: refill_per_key = base_per_gpu * num_allocated_gpus_for_org. Base_per_gpu ~= 60 tokens/s (tunable). That way when we add nodes the refill scales automatically.

Olivia: +1. Also add a small per-key grace buffer (e.g., 5 tokens) that is consumed before returning hard 429s; if grace exhausted, push requests into a short FIFO queue (100–500ms target), and only hard-drop if queue latency > sla. This avoids punting clients for brief spikes.

Maya: How do we compute num_allocated_gpus_for_org? per-org pool size or inferred from steady-state usage?

Li: Prefer: use configured org pool size when set (Reserved/Dedicated). Otherwise approximate by recent steady GPU-seconds consumed (moving avg over 5m) divided by per-gpu baseline. Sync value to admission proxies periodically (30s). Keep a safety floor of 1 GPU for new orgs.

Samir: Implementation concerns: local admission proxies must be cheap and not rely on global locks. We should avoid cross-proxy coordination on every admit. Suggest: local token buckets with periodic reconciliation to a central »alloc-store« (Kafka/consul). Reconciliation can move tokens in big chunks so short-term ops unaffected.

Olivia: Also: expose backpressure headers so SDKs can adapt: `X-Backpressure-Level: none|soft|hard`, `X-Estimated-Queue-ms`. Clients can backoff or switch fallback models.

Li: For fairness across keys in same org, use hierarchical buckets: org_bucket -> key_bucket. org_bucket enforces total across keys; key_bucket enforces per-key. If org_bucket is tight, we transition to fair-share mode where each active key gets min(cap_per_key, key_weight).

Samir: Edge cases: loadtests that hammer many keys. We should detect synthetic traffic (user-agent / token flags) and map to a separate admission class with stricter penalties (no grace queue).

Maya: Rollout? I'd do feature-flagged canary pushing to proxies in us-west only, and route 2% traffic for 24h, then 25%, then 100. Metric checks: 429 rate by org, queue latency P95, GPU utilization, failed requests.

Olivia: Telemetry to add: per-key token refill rate, tokens_consumed/s, grace_tokens_used, queue_push_count, queue_drop_count, and per-proxy reconciliation lag. Dashboards + alert thresholds (queue_drop_count > 5% for 10m).

Samir: Action items:
- Li: draft PR for capacity-proportional refill & hierarchical buckets (owner) — due EOD Fri.
- Olivia: schema for backpressure headers + SDK guidance (owner) — due Tue.
- Maya: create canary runbook + dashboard panels and alert thresholds (owner) — due Mon.
- Samir: add loadtest to replay the spike and validate (owner) — due Thu.

Maya: Sounds good. tagging @oncall as FYI when we flip canary. :eyes:

infra-bot: [AUTOMATED] saturation-alert acknowledged by oncall at 2026-03-18T12:38:02Z

Li: One more nuance: when nodes are being drained for maintenance, num_allocated_gpus should drop fast and refill should respect that — add a rapid-decay policy on reconciliation to avoid sudden overcommit.

Samir: OK let's keep the design doc light and iterate. I'll create the flag and a short spec in the repo. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
